abstract: The level of fatty acid unsaturation of chloroplast lipids is a key determinant of plant acclimation to different environmental stresses. Though the enzymes catalysing fatty acid desaturation are well known, the regulatory mechanisms linking their activity to environmental signals remain poorly understood. In this work, we have addressed the role of chloroplast 2-Cys peroxiredoxins (Prxs), thiol peroxidases that play a central role in redox regulation, in {omega}-3 fatty acid desaturation in lipids of the organelle, and their contribution to plant acclimation to environmental stress. Genetic and lipidomic analyses of Arabidopsis (Arabidopsis thaliana) mutants lacking 2-Cys Prxs and/or the chloroplast {omega}-3 fatty acid desaturases FAD7 and FAD8 revealed that 2-Cys Prxs are required for the efficient synthesis of trienoic fatty acids in thylakoid membrane lipids, particularly in phosphatidylglycerol (PG). Different approaches show the in vivo interaction of 2-Cys Prxs with FAD7 and FAD8. However, no redox changes of these desaturases were observed regardless the contents of 2-Cys Prxs, thus indicating a regulatory mechanism independent of the classical cysteine-based redox switch. The combined absence of 2-Cys Prxs and chloroplast {omega}-3 desaturases severely compromised recovery from high-light photoinhibition, indicating that both systems act concertedly to maintain photosystem II (PSII) function under stress. Together, our results uncover a novel role of 2-Cys Prxs controlling the level of chloroplast PG cis-unsaturation and raise the possibility that the chaperone/scaffold activity of these enzymes links membrane lipid remodelling to photosynthetic stress response.
